learn.rule: Signal words show how ideas connect: order (first, next, then, finally), addition (also, in addition), example (for example), contrast (however), result (as a result), conclusion (in conclusion).
learn.ruleEs: Las palabras de señal muestran cómo se conectan las ideas: orden (first, next, then, finally), adición (also, in addition), ejemplo (for example), contraste (however), resultado (as a result), conclusión (in conclusion).
learn.model: First, a seed soaks up water. Next, the seed swells and cracks open.
learn.notice: First and next put the steps in order. Each signal word is followed by a comma.

items.prompt: Choose the signal word that adds another fact about plants.
parts: Plants need sunlight to make food.
items.model: Plants need sunlight to make food. Also, they need water to grow.
items.why: Also adds one more fact to the same idea. However would show a contrast, and for example would start an example.
items.whyEs: Also agrega un dato más a la misma idea. However mostraría un contraste y for example empezaría un ejemplo.

items.prompt: Which signal word fits the blank in this sentence about whales?
items.text: Most mammals have thick fur. ____, whales have almost no hair.
items.why: However shows a contrast. Most mammals have thick fur, but whales do not.
items.whyEs: However muestra un contraste. La mayoría de los mamíferos tiene pelaje grueso, pero las ballenas no.

items.prompt: Put the sentences about a bean seed in order.
lines: First, the seed soaks up water from the soil.
Next, the seed coat splits open.
Then, a tiny root grows down into the soil.
Finally, a green shoot pushes up toward the light.
items.why: First begins the steps, next and then continue them, and finally ends them.
items.whyEs: First empieza los pasos, next y then los continúan y finally los termina.

items.prompt: Choose the signal words that fit this paragraph about animals in cold places.
parts: , Arctic foxes grow thick white fur in winter.
, they stay warm and hard to see in the snow.
items.model: Animals adapt to cold places. For example, Arctic foxes grow thick white fur in winter. As a result, they stay warm and hard to see in the snow.
items.why: For example introduces a case of adapting. As a result shows what the thick fur causes.
items.whyEs: For example presenta un caso de adaptación. As a result muestra lo que causa el pelaje grueso.

items.prompt: Check every sentence that uses a signal word to show contrast.

options.text: Bees visit flowers. As a result, flowers can make seeds.
Many insects are small. However, a stick insect can grow longer than a ruler.
Ants build nests. For example, some ants build nests underground.
Most snakes lay eggs. However, some snakes give birth to live young.

items.why: However shows a contrast. As a result shows what happens, and for example introduces an example.
items.whyEs: However muestra un contraste. As a result muestra lo que ocurre y for example presenta un ejemplo.

items.prompt: Which signal word fits best at the end of this paragraph about energy?
items.text: Plants make food from sunlight. Animals eat plants or other animals. ____, all living things depend on the Sun's energy.
items.why: In conclusion wraps up the whole paragraph with the big idea.
items.whyEs: In conclusion cierra todo el párrafo con la idea principal.

write.prompt: Write three sentences about how a plant or animal grows. Use First, Next, and Finally.
write.promptEs: Escribe tres oraciones sobre cómo crece una planta o un animal. Usa First, Next y Finally.
write.model: First, the tadpole hatches from an egg in the pond. Next, it grows back legs and front legs. Finally, it loses its tail and becomes a frog.

familyTalk.en: Tell the steps of making breakfast using first, next, and finally.
familyTalk.es: Cuenten los pasos para preparar el desayuno usando first, next y finally.

teacherTip.en: Hold up three fingers and have students say one sentence per finger, starting each with a signal word.
teacherTip.es: Levanta tres dedos y pide que los estudiantes digan una oración por dedo, empezando cada una con una palabra de señal.

sets.title: Why Towns Grow by Rivers
sets.titleEs: Por qué crecen los pueblos junto a los ríos

learn.rule: Signal words show how ideas connect: order (first, next, then, finally), addition (also, in addition), example (for example), contrast (however), result (as a result), conclusion (in conclusion).
learn.ruleEs: Las palabras de señal muestran cómo se conectan las ideas: orden (first, next, then, finally), adición (also, in addition), ejemplo (for example), contraste (however), resultado (as a result), conclusión (in conclusion).
learn.model: Rivers help towns grow. For example, boats carry goods from one town to another.
learn.notice: For example tells the reader that a specific case is coming.

items.prompt: Choose the signal word that gives an example about rivers.
parts: , boats carry goods from one town to another.
items.model: Rivers help towns grow. For example, boats carry goods from one town to another.
items.why: For example introduces a specific case of how rivers help. However and finally do not.
items.whyEs: For example presenta un caso específico de cómo ayudan los ríos. However y finally no lo hacen.

items.prompt: Which signal word shows a result in this railroad sentence?
items.text: The railroad reached the small town. ____, many new stores opened near the station.
items.why: As a result shows that the new stores happened because the railroad came.
items.whyEs: As a result muestra que las nuevas tiendas surgieron porque llegó el ferrocarril.

items.prompt: Put the sentences about a town meeting in order.
lines: First, neighbors gather in the school gym.
Next, the mayor explains the new park plan.
Then, people take turns asking questions.
Finally, everyone votes by raising a hand.
items.why: The signal words first, next, then, and finally make one order clear.
items.whyEs: Las palabras de señal first, next, then y finally dejan claro un solo orden.

items.prompt: Choose the signal words that fit this paragraph about libraries.
parts: Libraries serve a community in many ways.
, they lend books and offer free computers.
, they host story hours for children.
items.model: Libraries serve a community in many ways. For example, they lend books and offer free computers. In addition, they host story hours for children.
items.why: For example introduces the first case. In addition adds one more way libraries help.
items.whyEs: For example presenta el primer caso. In addition agrega otra manera en que ayudan las bibliotecas.

items.prompt: Check every sentence that uses a signal word to show addition.

options.text: The bridge was old. As a result, workers repaired it.
Volunteers cleaned the beach. Also, they planted dune grass.
The museum is free on Sundays. However, it costs five dollars on Saturdays.
The town built a new bus stop. In addition, it added a bike lane.

items.why: Also and in addition add another fact to the same idea. As a result and however do something different.
items.whyEs: Also e in addition agregan otro dato a la misma idea. As a result y however hacen algo distinto.

items.prompt: Which signal word fits best at the end of this paragraph about early cities?
items.text: Many early cities grew along rivers. Farmers had water for crops, and people could travel by boat. ____, rivers helped cities become centers of trade.
items.why: In conclusion sums up the paragraph's big idea.
items.whyEs: In conclusion resume la idea principal del párrafo.

write.prompt: Write four sentences about a place in your community. Use For example, Also, and As a result.
write.promptEs: Escribe cuatro oraciones sobre un lugar de tu comunidad. Usa For example, Also y As a result.
write.frame: Our park is important. For example, ___ Also, ___ As a result, ___

label: I used Also or In addition
Usé Also o In addition

write.model: Our town park is important to many families. For example, children play on the swings after school. Also, neighbors meet there on weekends. As a result, the park helps people feel connected.

familyTalk.en: Pick a place in your neighborhood and say why it matters. Use 'For example' and 'Also'.
familyTalk.es: Elijan un lugar de su vecindario y digan por qué es importante. Usen 'For example' y 'Also'.

teacherTip.en: Give each signal word a hand motion (add, example, result) and have students use the motion while reading aloud.
teacherTip.es: Asigna un gesto a cada palabra de señal (agregar, ejemplo, resultado) y pide que los estudiantes lo usen mientras leen en voz alta.

learn.rule: Signal words show how ideas connect: order (first, next, then, finally), addition (also, in addition), example (for example), contrast (however), result (as a result), conclusion (in conclusion).
learn.ruleEs: Las palabras de señal muestran cómo se conectan las ideas: orden (first, next, then, finally), adición (also, in addition), ejemplo (for example), contraste (however), resultado (as a result), conclusión (in conclusion).
learn.model: Ravi searched for an hour. However, the kite was nowhere to be seen.
learn.notice: However signals a turn in the story: Ravi hoped to find it, but he did not.

items.prompt: Choose the signal word that shows time order in this kite story.
parts: Ravi chased his kite across the field.
, he climbed the hill to get a better view.
items.model: Ravi chased his kite across the field. Then, he climbed the hill to get a better view.
items.why: Then shows what happened next in time. The other choices would not fit a sequence.
items.whyEs: Then muestra lo que pasó después en el tiempo. Las otras opciones no encajarían en una secuencia.

items.prompt: Which signal word shows a contrast in this kite sentence?
items.text: Ravi looked behind the fence. ____, the kite was not there.
items.why: However shows that things did not go as hoped. Ravi looked, but the kite was still missing.
items.whyEs: However muestra que las cosas no salieron como se esperaba. Ravi miró, pero la cometa seguía perdida.

items.prompt: Put the story sentences about the kite in order.
lines: First, Ravi tied a long red string to his kite.
Next, a strong wind lifted the kite high above the field.
Then, the string snapped and the kite floated away.
Finally, a neighbor found it caught in a tree and brought it back.
items.why: First, next, then, and finally mark the order of events in a story.
items.whyEs: First, next, then y finally marcan el orden de los sucesos en un cuento.

items.prompt: Choose the signal words that fit this part of the story.
parts: , his sister stayed calm and made a plan.
, they found the kite before dark.
items.model: Ravi felt worried. However, his sister stayed calm and made a plan. As a result, they found the kite before dark.
items.why: However shows the sister's calm is different from Ravi's worry. As a result shows the plan led to finding the kite.
items.whyEs: However muestra que la calma de la hermana es distinta de la preocupación de Ravi. As a result muestra que el plan llevó a encontrar la cometa.

items.prompt: Check every sentence that uses a signal word to show an example.

options.text: The ending surprised me. However, my brother guessed it.
Good stories have strong characters. For example, Mia is brave and funny.
The book was long. As a result, it took me a week to read.
Authors use sensory details. For example, one writer describes the smell of rain.

items.why: For example introduces a specific case. However shows a contrast, and as a result shows a result.
items.whyEs: For example presenta un caso específico. However muestra un contraste y as a result muestra un resultado.

items.prompt: Which signal word fits best in this detective sentence?
items.text: The detective found muddy footprints. She also found a torn glove. ____, she knew the thief had left through the garden.
items.why: As a result shows that her conclusion came from the clues she found.
items.whyEs: As a result muestra que su conclusión vino de las pistas que encontró.

write.prompt: Write three sentences about a time you lost or found something. Use First, However, and Finally.
write.promptEs: Escribe tres oraciones sobre una vez que perdiste o encontraste algo. Usa First, However y Finally.
write.model: First, I looked under my bed for my missing shoe. However, it was not there. Finally, I found it in the dog's basket.

familyTalk.en: Tell a short story about something you found. Use first, however, and finally.
familyTalk.es: Cuenten una historia corta sobre algo que encontraron. Usen first, however y finally.

teacherTip.en: Read a short story aloud and have students raise a hand each time they hear a signal word.
teacherTip.es: Lee un cuento corto en voz alta y pide que los estudiantes levanten la mano cada vez que oigan una palabra de señal.
